topics.title: Git and GitHub
topics.description: Own your changes, integrate with teammates, and ship through a reviewed GitHub workflow.
topics.prerequisite: Comfort editing a small program. No Git experience required.

modules.title: Own a project with Git
modules.story: You maintain a device-diagnostics repository. Ship a requested LED timing change without losing unrelated work or sharing accidental edits.
modules.outcome: Produce a reviewed checkpoint, explain its scope, and choose the right recovery operation.

lessons.title: Put your own project under version control
lessons.context: Start with a pristine project folder and record a baseline before reviewing any AI edits.

lessons.title: Review the requested change
lessons.context: The timing request should change implementation and test, while preserving the setup instructions.

lessons.title: Capture the right version
lessons.context: A follow-up edit arrives after you have staged the intended change.

lessons.title: Create and back up a checkpoint
lessons.context: Check the intended snapshot and share your experiment branch as a solo maintainer.

lessons.title: Recover without losing the wrong work
lessons.context: Before another engineer joins, explain exactly which layer each undo operation affects.

modules.title: Integrate a teammate’s work
modules.story: You add a status report while a teammate fixes the sampler. Keep both changes, investigate a conflicting setting, and hand back a tested branch.
modules.outcome: Integrate another engineer’s commits without confusing remote state, working files, or a resolved conflict.

lessons.title: Two engineers, one starting point
lessons.context: Your status-report feature and the teammate’s sampler fix start from the same commit.

lessons.title: Learn what changed remotely
lessons.context: The teammate has pushed a fix; your clone still knows the old remote tip.

lessons.title: Resolve the requirement, not just the text
lessons.context: Both branches edited one interval, but the real requirements concern two different jobs.

lessons.title: Share an integrated result
lessons.context: A clean file is not enough: check both behaviors and tell the next engineer what changed.

modules.title: Ship with GitHub and AI
modules.story: The team needs a bounded sample-count setting. Turn the issue into an AI request, inspect the proposal, repair a CI failure, and prepare a reviewable release.
modules.outcome: Use GitHub’s project, review, automation, and release surfaces while remaining responsible for AI-generated changes.

lessons.title: Find the right place on GitHub
lessons.context: Start with an issue, not a vague request to rewrite the repository.

lessons.title: Give AI a bounded engineering task
lessons.context: The requested range is 1 through 10 samples, inclusive; unrelated files and secrets are outside scope.

lessons.title: Review evidence from a new commit
lessons.context: The AI proposal passes a weak test but rejects the valid upper boundary.

lessons.title: Finish the handoff, not just the chat
lessons.context: Review and automation must refer to the current commit before you merge and describe the release.

topics.title: STM32 to Zynq 7000
topics.description: Take over a project, coordinate hardware and software, and deliver something a teammate can reproduce.
topics.prerequisite: Basic STM32 editing, compiling, and downloading experience.

modules.title: Take over an embedded project
modules.story: You join the board-diagnostics project with STM32 experience. Identify the execution roles, follow the files, and prepare a source set another engineer can rebuild.
modules.outcome: Explain the Processing System (PS) and Programmable Logic (PL) and the producer, consumer, and ownership of the project’s important artifacts.

lessons.title: Explore software execution and digital logic
lessons.context: First establish which changes run as CPU software and which describe hardware.

lessons.title: Follow each artifact to its reader
lessons.context: The project tree contains application code, generated support, and hardware handoffs.

lessons.title: Give the next engineer reproducible sources
lessons.context: The team policy keeps maintained source and settings in Git, with versioned build artifacts supplied separately.

modules.title: Coordinate a hardware change
modules.story: The diagnostics application gains a GPIO status interface. Coordinate a software-only edit, the changed hardware contract, and the matching files loaded for testing.
modules.outcome: Repair stale support data and verify that the application, handoff, and loaded hardware belong to the same design.

lessons.title: Make the software-only change
lessons.context: Begin with a new greeting so you can isolate the application build and load path.

lessons.title: Bring in the changed hardware contract
lessons.context: A teammate changes the software-visible GPIO interface; rebuilding against old support data is insufficient.

lessons.title: Load the artifacts you actually built
lessons.context: The v2 host files are ready, while the illustrated board still holds v1.

lessons.title: Review a teammate’s handoff package
lessons.context: Before accepting the package, compare the hardware revision used by every consumer.

modules.title: Deliver and diagnose a build
modules.story: Your integration run succeeds, but the next engineer needs to reproduce it after a power cycle. Investigate failures by layer and prepare a delivery with traceable evidence.
modules.outcome: Distinguish run from boot, diagnose the first mismatched layer, and assemble a reproducible teammate handoff.

lessons.title: Check what happens after power-on
lessons.context: A JTAG-loaded program can differ from the persistent boot setup.

lessons.title: Find the first failing layer
lessons.context: Use observations to distinguish a stale build, an old load, and an old boot setup.

lessons.title: Prepare a reproducible delivery
lessons.context: A zip named final is not a reproducible handoff; connect sources, artifacts, versions, and observations.
